quote: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
source: Annie Dillard, The Writing Life, chapter 2 (1989)

evidence.where: Both archive.org scans of the book (Harper and Row 1989, HarperPerennial 1990) are lending-restricted and their search-inside was refused, so the book itself was not read. Wording checked against Wikiquote’s Writing Life entry and The Marginalian’s block quotation of the passage, which agree exactly; the chapter confirmed from a chapter-by-chapter study guide that places the schedules passage (“chaos and whim”) in chapter 2
evidence.edition: The Writing Life (New York: Harper and Row, 1989)
evidence.locator: Chapter 2, opening the paragraph on schedules: followed by “What we do with this hour, and that one, is what we are doing. A schedule defends from chaos and whim.” The proposer’s p. 32 matches my memory of how the line is cited but was not confirmed against a scan, so the page is left out of the shipped source

reason: The sentence is unquestionably Dillard’s and from The Writing Life, in this exact wording in every transcription of the passage; the chapter is corroborated, the page is not, so the source ships with chapter and year only. The shipped Makers line of hers is a different sentence; shipped.js finds no match and she has no Classics entry. Not banned.
